function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

I’m sorry, but I don’t have real‑time market data.  The most reliable way to get the current spot price of gold in the United States is to check one of the following:

| Source | How to access |
|--------|---------------|
| **Kitco** | https://www.kitco.com/ – “Gold” page shows the live spot price in USD per troy ounce. |
| **Bloomberg** | https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/commodities – search “Gold” for the live price. |
| **Reuters** | https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities – “Gold” ticker shows the current price. |
| **NYMEX / COMEX** | https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/metals/precious.html – the official exchange price. |
| **Financial news apps** (e.g., CNBC, Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance) – search “Gold” or “XAU/USD”. |

If you need the price for a specific time or a historical snapshot, let me know and I can show you how to retrieve it programmatically (e.g., via an API such as the Metals-API or Quandl).
